gaps.sentence: He found ___ coin buried in the sand.
gaps.explanation: 'A coin' first mention; 'in the sand' — sand as a mass takes 'the' here (the sand on that beach).

gaps.sentence: He's always been fascinated by ___ universe.
My uncle is ___ university lecturer and a painter in his free time.
gaps.explanation: 'A university lecturer' (the u sounds like /juː/); the second gap is also 'an artist'.

gaps.sentence: He was offered ___ job in the human resources department.
gaps.explanation: 'A job' — first mention of one of many possible jobs. Note: 'in human resources' takes no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ water in this bottle tastes strange.
gaps.explanation: The of/in-phrase makes the noun definite: the water in this bottle.

gaps.sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
gaps.explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).

gaps.sentence: These apples cost two euros ___ kilo.
gaps.explanation: 'A/per' is used for rates: two euros a kilo, twice a week, 60 km an hour.

gaps.sentence: ___ Smith family have lived in this street since 1990.
gaps.explanation: 'The Smith family' — the whole family takes 'the'.
